Back in 1989, our Chairman, Osman ‘Ozzie’ Ertosun built his first care home – a small nursing home in Catford, South London – with his father. Since then, he and his team have grown our organisation to the 31 care homes and homecare service we are proud to be today. Our care homes are a combination of homes we've acquired and homes we’ve built ourselves. Every new design is based on the knowledge we’ve gained from our valuable experience. This helps us make our care homes the very best they can be for the people who call them their home. Family at our heart Family really does mean everything to us – it underpins our whole organisation. Whether it’s the people we care for, their families and friends or our team members – they are all part of our extended family. Our family values empower us to deliver empathetic, compassionate person-centred care. Quite simply, it’s the same care we would want our own loved ones to receive. As well as providing excellent care and a high quality of life to the people who live with us, we strive to create welcoming and relaxed environments. We want everyone to belong, and enjoy days filled with purpose and meaning, in a place they are proud to call ‘home’. About our approach Dedicated team members We couldn’t achieve our goals without our committed team members! They are all carefully selected for their experience, skills and caring natures. Above all else, we look for people who share our passion and values. It goes without saying that we are rigorous in meeting all regulations and safeguarding requirements. Protecting the people who live with us is our top priority. Meet our team Support when you need it most We are here to guide you through the process of selecting the right care home and a package that meets your loved one’s needs. Sometimes, as you look at the vast choice of care homes, it may feel confusing or overwhelming. That is why we are happy to help at every stage of a family’s journey and take care to outline our approach in everything we do. We will always provide the right type of care, in the right place, for yourself, or a precious person in your life, and we will always meet people’s needs on their own terms – not ours. Our story Our approach Our team Awards Life with us Types of care Respite and Short-Term Breaks Residential Care Nursing Care Dementia Care End-of-life Care Day care Wellbeing Help & advice Help & advice Choosing a care home Day to day life Funding your care Your Move-in Experience Resources Careers Careers Care home roles Regional support roles Domiciliary care roles Support office roles Professionals News & events Contact us Contact us General enquiry Your voice matters Dovecote Manor Celebrates 103rd Birthday of War-Time Nurse Connie 01 May 2026Share The care home community at Dovecote Manor recently came together to celebrate a remarkable life milestone – Connie’s 103rd Birthday! This incredibly special occasion was marked by a party attended by her family and friends. It was a wonderful way to celebrate Connie’s long, fulfilling life and all that she has achieved. At just 17 years old, during the beginning of World War II, Connie began nursing soldiers. At the time, nurses were carefully selected - they had to be unmarried and without children, ready to devote themselves fully to the immense demands of wartime care. After the war, Connie went on to build a loving family life. She is a proud mother of two boys and was married to her beloved husband, Harold, for 52 years. The loving bond they shared now lives on through the memories and stories that Connie tells her friends at Dovecote Manor. Connie’s family legacy of caring for others has been passed through generations. Connie’s mother, grandmother, and aunties were all midwives and nurses. This legacy continues to this day, as Connie’s granddaughter is now training to become a biomedical scientist, carrying on the family’s passion for healthcare. Those who know Connie describe her as a kind, gentle, and caring person, someone who has always put others before herself. These qualities were evident throughout her life and continue to shine through today. Her birthday was filled with warmth, smiles, and heartfelt celebrations, as everyone at Dovecote Manor felt privileged to honour such an inspiring woman and the extraordinary life she has lived. Connie’s story is a powerful reminder of the strength, dedication, and quiet heroism of a generation whose care and sacrifice shaped the world we live in today.
